newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn reduces share offering size.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn reduces share offering size.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp on Friday said it filed a final short form prospectus with Canadian and U.S. regulators for an offering of 7.5 million subordinate voting shares.
The Toronto-based real estate company said it changed its original plan to issue 12.5 million shares because of poor market conditions.
"In management's view, adverse market conditions resulted in the current share price not adequately reflecting the growth prospects for the company," TrizecHahn said in a release.
With a price of US$20 per share, the reduced issue represents gross proceeds of US$150 million for TrizecHahn.

The company said the offering accomplished TrizecHahn's principal objectives by supplementing its capital, increasing its visibility and broadening its institutional ownership, particularly in the United States.
The offering is scheduled to close on April 30, 1997.

TrizecHahn said the proceeds of the offering will be used for general corporate purposes, including the acquistion of office properties, development of retail properties and repaying debt. The debt repayment includes the redemption of a portion of the 10.875 percent senior notes due October 2005 of Trizec Finance Ltd.

TrizecHahn shares have fallen more than 15 percent since reaching a 52-week high of C$33.30 on February 11. The shares closed at C$30.25 on March 24 when the company first announced the planned offering of 12.5 million shares.
Shares of TrizecHahn were down C$0.35 to C$27.95 in late morning trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. More than 62,000 shares changed hands.

Based in Toronto, TrizecHahn is one of North America's largest publicly traded real estate companies, with interests in 68 income-producing properties. The company is listed in Toronto, New York and Montreal.
